data.one_liner: Easy to use and customizable Theme Provider with persistence and dynamic switching.
data.what_it_does: Provides app color schemes throughout the widget tree, automatically rebuilds the UI dynamically when themes change, and optionally persists user theme preferences to disk using shared preferences.
use_when: You want a straightforward way to manage and persist light/dark or custom themes in a Flutter app.
You need to provide theme-specific options alongside your theme data.
avoid_when: You are already using a state management solution like Riverpod or Bloc that handles theme state directly.
You require complex reactive system theme listening out of the box without manual setup callbacks.
strengths: Easy setup for multi-theme apps with custom theme IDs and descriptions
Built-in disk persistence via shared preferences
Includes helper widgets like theme cycling icon buttons and selection dialogs
weaknesses: Does not dynamically listen to system theme changes automatically out of the box on start without custom callbacks
Requires wrapping routes or the material app with specific consumer widgets

alternatives.name: provider
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer a general-purpose state management solution that can also handle theme state.

alternatives.name: riverpod
alternatives.why_pick_it: For a robust, compile-safe state management approach to handle application themes.

alternatives.name: bloc
alternatives.why_pick_it: If your app is already architected around BLoC and you want event-driven theme changes.
